states.name: caret
states.gap: The caret sits 3px (1.5 CSS px) low against its own type: cap top 111, baseline 142, so the optical centre is 126.5, but the caret centre is 129.5 — A's is off by only 1px. B's square caps make that misalignment legible instead of hiding it: the bar overshoots the cap line by 18px and drops 15px past the descender with dead-blunt corners at both ends.
states.gapTheirs: The caret is not pixel-snapped: it is anti-aliased on all four sides — left edge #31CAFE (~80% coverage), right edge #C7ECF8 (~22%), caps fading through #77DAFC — so its effective width is ~3.2px with an indeterminate boundary, versus B's hard #00BFFF from x357 through x362 with zero anti-aliasing. On top of that A domes the terminals with a ~1.5 device px (0.75 CSS px) cap radius, turning a 3px caret into a lozenge against a mono face whose glyph terminals are all flat.
states.verdict: B wins on the only thing a caret has to do: be a crisp edge. A's caret is soft on every side — an 80%-alpha left edge and a 22%-alpha right edge mean you cannot say where the insertion point actually is, and at 1x that fuzz doubles into a smear; the rounded pill caps are the wrong terminal shape for a squared-off mono face. B's is a hard, honest hairline, though it is seated 1.5 CSS px below the optical centre of its line and its blunt corners advertise the fact. Neither is a precise instrument: both run the caret to the full 74px line box, 2.4× the 30–32px cap height, so what you get is a fence post standing in the text, not a nib.

Caret-to-glyph gaps are identical in both: 1px (0.5 CSS px) clear of the preceding 'l', 0px clear of the following 'a' — the caret touches the next glyph in each

states.name: unfocused
states.gap: Only 2 device px (1 CSS px) of clearance between the 's' ink terminal (ends x=1940) and the caret (starts x=1943), against A's 7 device px — B right-aligns the caret to the advance boundary so it sits inside the cell it just left, giving side bearings of 2px left / 25px right (12.5:1 lopsided vs A's 7/18, 2.6:1). At normal size the caret reads as a blue tail welded to the 's', not a separate instrument.
states.gapTheirs: Caret sits 3 device px above the optical centre of its glyph band — 22px of overhang above the ascender against 15px below the descender — and is drawn entirely to the right of the advance boundary (left edge at x=1930, boundary at ~1929.5), so it floats inside the following space cell instead of straddling the insertion point; it is also the taller of the two bars, 76px over a 29px ascender (2.62x) vs B's 74px (2.55x).
states.verdict: Both ship the same caret and both get it wrong: a 3px pale sky-blue bar stretched to the full line box — 76px and 74px against a 29px ascender, roughly 2.6x — so the insertion point is a highlighter stripe where a hairline belongs, and at #AEE5FB on #F9F9F9 it is the faintest mark on a page where it is the one thing that must be instantly findable. Neither image shows a selection at all, so selection colour is simply untested in both. A wins on the one thing that separates them: it leaves 7 device px of air after the 's' instead of B's 2, where B's caret grazes the letter and reads as a blue terminal on the glyph. That is a slight win on a dimension where both are wrong.
